# Introduction

scdRs is a native R implementation of scDRS (single-cell
disease-relevance score; Zhang, Hou et al., *Nature Genetics* 2022). It
scores each cell of a single-cell RNA-seq data set for excess expression
of a disease gene set (e.g. from GWAS) compared with matched control gene
sets.

The package is under development. This vignette will describe the full
workflow once it is implemented.

# Installation

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages("BiocManager")
}
BiocManager::install("scdRs")
```

# Example data

The package ships the toy data of the original scDRS (2,500 mouse genes,
30 cells) as a `SingleCellExperiment`.

```{r toydata, message = FALSE}
library(scdRs)
sce <- scdrsLoadToyData()
sce
table(sce$cell_type)
```

The disease gene sets are stored in the scDRS `.gs` format: one trait
per line, with a comma-separated list of genes.

```{r genesets}
gs <- read.delim(system.file("extdata", "toydata_mouse.gs",
    package = "scdRs"))
gs$TRAIT
length(strsplit(gs$GENESET, ",")[[1]])
```

# Preprocessing

`scdrsPreprocess()` regresses covariates out of the log-normalized data
(here one covariate stored in `colData`) and computes the gene statistics
used to choose control genes. With a sparse assay the correction is done
implicitly, so the data stays sparse; the input assay is never changed.

```{r preprocess}
sce <- scdrsPreprocess(sce, cov = "covariate")
rowData(sce)[1:5, c("scdrs_mean", "scdrs_var", "scdrs_var_tech",
    "scdrs_mean_var")]
head(colData(sce)[, c("scdrs_mean", "scdrs_var")])
```

# Citation

If you use scdRs, please cite the original scDRS paper:

```{r citation}
citation("scdRs")
```
